internal_decisions: Names are untrusted, so upload_path raises ValueError for names that would leave base or resolve to base itself: '..' escapes, a leading '/', backslashes, NUL bytes, '.'. The contract only specifies ValueError for empty names, so this goes beyond it.
'a/../b' stays inside base, so it is allowed and normalised to <base>/b.

defects.repro: upload_path('/b', 'a\\b.txt') raises ValueError('invalid name'). The contract only allows ValueError for an empty or whitespace-only name. Test: test_d1_backslash_name_is_ordinary.
defects.fix: Either allow a backslash, which is a normal file-name character on POSIX, or add the rejection to the section 6 contract. Rejecting it is probably the safer behaviour, so updating the contract is the better fix.
defects.if_skipped: A legitimate upload whose name contains a backslash is refused. The behaviour is also undocumented.

defects.repro: Catalogue.find('ann', 'y'*60000) raises sqlite3.OperationalError: LIKE or GLOB pattern too complex. SQLite's LIKE pattern limit is about 50 KB. Test: test_d2_long_search_text_no_crash.
defects.fix: Check the length of the search text, or use instr(lower(name), lower(?)) > 0 instead of LIKE. Note that lower() folds ASCII only, which matches the contract. Alternatively, raise ValueError for text over a stated limit.
defects.if_skipped: An untrusted user can submit a long search string and cause an unhandled sqlite3 exception, which crashes the request.

gaps: Concurrency and multi-thread use of the sqlite connection were not tested; the architecture gives no contract for it.
Symlink behaviour in upload_path was not tested. Section 2 lists writing files to disk as out of scope, so the function only builds strings.

advisory.problem: The contract says the path is kept inside `base` and the brief says names come from untrusted users. No test uses a traversal name (`../x`, `a/../../x`) or an absolute name (`/etc/passwd`). The ACs do not cover this either, so the tests do not pin the behaviour.
advisory.evidence: `return os.path.abspath(os.path.join(base, name))` after a strip check passes all three storage tests and lets `../../etc/passwd` escape `base`.

advisory.problem: No test changes a token that has the right secret, for example by altering the payload or expiry or truncating the signature. AC-006 only covers a foreign secret and three short junk strings. A weak or partial MAC is not caught.
advisory.evidence: A token that signs only the file id, or compares only a prefix of the MAC, passes every token test. Forged expiries are accepted.

advisory.problem: No test uses a search text with quote or SQL characters, and no test checks that `find` stays within one owner when the text matches names of another owner. AC-010 covers a different owner with `""` only.
advisory.evidence: A `find` that builds SQL by string formatting passes all catalogue tests. A `find` that ignores the owner when `text` is non-empty also passes.

advisory.problem: AC-006 requires that no exception other than `InvalidToken` is raised for a malformed string. The tests cover only `""`, `"abc"` and `"a.b.c"`. Non-base64 or non-ASCII input is not tried.
advisory.evidence: A parser that raises `binascii.Error` or `UnicodeDecodeError` on other malformed input passes all of these cases.
